subject: Interaction between snapshot restores and scheduled delete waves — quick Q&A
messages:
From: Sara Ng <sara.ng@blueharbor.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+legal@blueharbor.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Restore question: will scheduled delete waves re-apply after an on-demand restore?

Hi Mina,

Quick operational question as we're finalizing the DR runbook: if BlueHarbor triggers an on-demand restore of a snapshot (to recover recent records for investigation), will the platform's scheduled deletion waves (the periodic expunge that permanently removes tombstoned objects) still run against those restored objects after the restore completes? Our security/compliance team is worried that a restore could reintroduce data that then gets swept a few hours later.

Specific asks:
- Does a restore re-create tombstone metadata / original deletion timestamps?
- Is there any guard to prevent an immediate subsequent expunge of a restored object?
- If we need to hold data for legal/retention reasons post-restore, what's the recommended approach?

We have a compliance window where restored data must be preserved for 30 days after restore for investigations. Attaching the retention policy excerpt.

Thanks,
Sara
Ops & Legal
BlueHarbor Bank

Attachment: retention-policy-summary.pdf (pdf, 92KB)

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Sara Ng <sara.ng@blueharbor.com>
Cc: ops+legal@blueharbor.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Restore question: will scheduled delete waves re-apply after an on-demand restore?

Hi Sara — great questions, thanks for flagging. Short answers up front, then notes and recommended actions.

Short answers:
- Restore does NOT resurrect tombstone records with their original expunge timestamps. Restores create a fresh object record with a new creation timestamp; the original tombstone is not re-attached.
- The scheduled expunge (delete) waves run over objects that currently have tombstone markers / TTLs set. Because restores create a fresh object without a tombstone, they are not immediately eligible for the next expunge wave.
- For compliance/holds, the recommended approach is to attach a temporary retention tag (legal_hold or investigation_hold) on the restored object; that tag extends or overrides expunge eligibility for the duration of the hold.

Key details / caveats:
- If a restore is performed by re-hydrating from an older snapshot that includes the tombstone metadata (rare, but possible for full-volume restores), then the tombstone metadata could be present. Our hosted default restore path intentionally strips tombstone markers to avoid re-triggering expunge, but on-prem V1 tooling may preserve metadata — please confirm if you are using our Private appliance.

- Expunge waves are driven by two signals: tombstone marker + expunge-eligible timestamp. The waves ignore objects without a tombstone. We also run a separate consistency pass that looks for orphaned metadata; restored objects with no tombstone are skipped.

Recommended runbook steps for BlueHarbor:
1) After any on-demand restore, immediately call the API to set a short-term investigation_hold tag (we can provide a script).
2) If you need the restored data to be immutable for 30 days, set retention_days=30 on the tag; the platform will prevent a downstream expunge while the tag is active.
3) If you plan to snapshot the restored dataset back into your long-term archive, request a special snapshot that strips expunge metadata (we can coordinate).

I've attached our sample restore playbook (lightweight script + example API calls). If you'd like, we can schedule 30 minutes with engineering to walk through a mock restore and show the expunge wave log entries.

--
Mina Haddad
Sr. PM, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-restore-playbook.md (text, 6KB); internal link: https://drive.redwood.internal/Shared/KB/backup-retention-v2

Subject: Re: Restore question: will scheduled delete waves re-apply after an on-demand restore?

Technical addendum from engineering — timeline and implementation details:

- Our restore pipeline (hosted) performs metadata normalization: it strips tombstone markers and resets the last_modified/created timestamps to the restore time. This is by design to avoid accidental expunge.
- Expunge waves run every 6 hours on the primary region; there is also a weekly background compaction that permanently frees disk blocks. If a restore occurs between an expunge and the next compaction, the restored object will still be safe because it lacks a tombstone.
- For Private installs on older images (<= v1.3.1), the default CLI restore preserves tombstones. We recommend running the migration script (cli-tool migrate-restore-metadata --strip-tombstone) or upgrading to >= v1.4.0.

Operational best practices we propose for customers:
1) Use the API call: POST /v1/objects/{id}/tags with payload {"tag":"investigation_hold","ttl_days":30} immediately after restore. (We'll provide the curl snippet.)
2) Add a post-restore audit webhook to your orchestration that notifies both ops and compliance teams; that webhook event includes the new object_id and the retention tag id.
3) For cases where BlueHarbor wants guaranteed immutability for 30 days, create a short-lived snapshot (retention tag applied) and mark it as immutable in the console.

I'll attach a sample curl snippet and we can post it to the KB.

- Aditya (Infra SE)
